evidence: Eleven work nodes each held passages belonging to several DIFFERENT works, and check_kg_work_id_uniqueness.py reported them as "KNOWN (allowlisted) ... remediation pending" and PASSED, so the defect survived every previous audit. ~3,350 passages answered "which work is this from?" with the wrong work. Worst cases: Seneca Epistulae Morales (2,135 passages) filed under De Providentia; Aristotle Magna Moralia (434), Eudemian Ethics (41) and Physics (71) under Nicomachean Ethics; Epicurus Letters and Fragments (193) under Epictetus Fragments; Plato Apology (125) under Republic; five Theological Orations of Gregory of Nazianzus (115), Evodius De fide (36) and three further Augustine works (86) under De Libero Arbitrio; Plutarch De Stoicorum Repugnantiis (47) and De communibus notitiis (6) under Pseudo-Plutarch De Fato; Aristotle De anima (30) under De interpretatione; Justin Second Apology (15) under First Apology; Didache (6) under Epistula Barnabae; Calcidius (5) under Plato Timaeus; Gellius Noctes Atticae (1) under Diogenes Laertius.
proposed_action: APPLIED (scripts/apply_2026_08_17_work_conflation.py). 3,087 passages were double-parented — already under their correct work AND under the conflated one — so the wrong edge was deleted with the correct parent verified to remain. 259 were single-parented: 37 re-parented to work nodes that already existed but sat empty (De Correptione et Gratia, Justin Second Apology, Gellius NA VII.2) and 222 to 9 work nodes created from the passages' own author / work_title / language / work_canonical_id. check_kg_work_id_uniqueness now reports "OK: every kg_work_id maps to a single canonical work". No passage lost a parent.

evidence: Origen's Exhortation to Martyrdom held 51 passages and every one of them was Clement of Alexandria's Protrepticus (passage_clement_protr_*) — a title collision on "Exhortation", the same failure mode as the Alcinous/Hegesippus case. Invisible to the conflation check because the node was internally consistent: 100% foreign but from a single work, so it looked "pure".
proposed_action: APPLIED. All 51 were already parented to work_clement_protrepticus, so the edges to Origen were deleted. Origen's Exhortation now correctly shows no ingested text and is flagged needs_text_ingestion.

evidence: Exposed only by splitting the conflated works: passages had inherited their HOST work's author. 115 passages of Gregory of Nazianzus' Theological Orations were authored_by Augustine of Hippo; 36 passages of Evodius' De fide contra Manichaeos were authored_by Augustine; 1 passage of Gellius' Noctes Atticae was authored_by Diogenes Laertius; 38 passages of the pseudonymous De Fato were authored_by Plutarch of Chaeronea although the work node's own description sets out why it is not his.
proposed_action: APPLIED. authored_by edges and metadata.author repointed to the author named by each passage's own label and canonical id. For De Fato the manuscript attribution is preserved in metadata.manuscript_attribution rather than asserted as authorship.

evidence: The ontology defines influences as "source intellectually influences target". Eleven person->person edges asserted the reverse: Calvin influences Augustine, Luther influences Augustine, Edwards influences Augustine and Locke, Lucretius influences Epicurus, Boethius influences Aristotle and Plato, Maimonides influences Avicenna, Gersonides influences Averroes, Jansen influences Luther, Cyril of Alexandria influences Irenaeus. Checked against the dates in the node ids, 22 comparable edges run early->late.
proposed_action: APPLIED. Each predicate changed to its declared inverse influenced_by, keeping the same pair and arrow. Two further chronology alerts were checked and are FALSE POSITIVES recorded in the data module so a later pass does not "fix" them: Augustine critiques Julian of Eclanum (contemporaries, Contra Iulianum is real) and Irenaeus precedes Bardaisan (correct; the alert came from a mis-parsed floruit).

evidence: 445 Plato passages carried a literal '?' in their CTS URN, e.g. urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0059.tlg002.perseus-grc2:?.17a. "?" is a reserved URI character, so every one of these URNs was unresolvable — they are the project's FAIR identifiers.
proposed_action: APPLIED. The empty '?.' segment was removed. All 445 belong to Plato works cited by flat Stephanus pagination (Apology, Phaedo, Phaedrus), which have no book division, so the canonical Perseus form is …perseus-grc2:17a. The Stephanus reference itself was not touched.

evidence: person_salles_ricardo_contemporary had period "Modern" with birth_date "fl. 21st c."; person_celestius_d430s stored a floruit ("fl. early 5th c. CE") in birth_date, which made birth appear to fall after death (c. 430 CE).
proposed_action: APPLIED. Period corrected to Contemporary; the floruit moved to its own field.

evidence: CLAUDE.md lists five canonical periods (Presocratic, Classical, Hellenistic, Imperial, Late Antiquity) but the graph uses a wider vocabulary: "Roman Imperial" 11,220, "Late Antiquity" 2,405, "Classical Greek" 2,089, "Contemporary" 1,433, "Patristic" 1,361, "Hellenistic" 469, "Roman Republican" 408, "Modern" 363, "Early Modern" 79, "Medieval" 54, "Second Temple Judaism" 29, "Presocratic" 13, "Cross-period" 11, "Rabbinic" 2, "First Temple / Pre-exilic Judaism" 2, and 85 nulls.
proposed_action: NO DATA CHANGE. The first pass proposed normalising "Classical Greek" to "Classical"; checked before applying, that value is carried by 2,089 nodes and is a coherent established label, and the other non-listed values are legitimate scholarly periods. This is a taxonomy decision for the maintainer, not a factual error. Either widen the list in CLAUDE.md to match the data, or decide a controlled vocabulary and migrate deliberately.

evidence: After the four waves the factual scan returns 4 alerts, each verified benign: 2 chronology alerts (Augustine/Julian, Irenaeus/Bardaisan — both real relations, flagged by date-parsing heuristics); 1 lifespan alert (Hillel the Elder, c. 110 BCE - c. 10 CE, the traditional 120-year lifespan, not a data error); 1 CTS shape (urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0076c.stoa001 for Cassian, a textgroup id with a letter suffix that the validator regex does not model rather than a malformed URN).
